task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: PNR fail as a defensive-response trigger
PULL_UP shot as a candidate counter
methodological_questions: What defines a PNR-fail trigger and a unit, so that the 70% and 2pp thresholds are measurable?
Is the lift measured against a matched comparison that controls for shot quality, score state and personnel?
Do the retrieved A1, SHOULD-counter and TOV_FORCE records show that similar counter-effect claims survive selection, label-error and regression-to-the-mean checks?
Can a within-unit, out-of-season test separate a real counter from artifacts?

historical_evidence.finding: Record states the A1 adapter PPP lift was tested with asymmetry, confidence and carryover checks. Reported T1 dPPP: adapter +0.0667 (n=205), neutral +0.0248 (n=50), no_signal +0.1260 (n=57), wrong_way +0.0111 (n=274). T2 adapter minus no-signal was -0.0361 (1 vote) and -0.1170 (2 votes). T3 next-game PPP gave Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842. Failure mechanism recorded as C_artifact. Limitations listed: label or classification error, selection or regression to the mean, label-error risk, mechanical-floor risk.

Record states a within-scheme re-test controlling for early-third PPP quintiles. Within-scheme gap: DROP +0.0830 (Welch p=0.0046), HELP +0.0539 (p=0.0493), SWITCH -0.0199 (p=0.6514). Quintile gaps were mixed in sign (-0.0440, -0.0231, +0.0138, +0.0133, +0.0966). Carryover gaps were small and not clearly positive. Failure mechanism recorded as E_unclear.

Record states within-game adaptation toward SHOULD-counter play types was associated with higher later PPP: adapters +0.0701 (n=239) vs non-adapters +0.0121 (n=269), advantage +0.0580. Subgroups: DROP +0.1001, SWITCH -0.0436, HELP +0.0450. A later run gave adapter minus non-adapter +0.048 (p=0.0199), with the SWITCH subgroup reversed. Limitation recorded: selection or regression to the mean.

Record covers a TOV_FORCE 3-ply adversarial test on 4 games and 8 offense-defense sides. Raw R1 lifts shrank by about half under opponent re-route and PT-shift controls (e.g., ORL +8.4 to net +3.7pp; PHI +12.0 to +6.0). Record states net lift is model-implied rather than observed in games, and the verdict is descriptive. It is related to [prior work][prior work] and measures turnovers.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Scheme-adaptation counter effect (A1 adapter PPP lift) tested for asymmetry, scheme-vote confidence and next-game carryover
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact. Wrong-way and no-signal comparisons did not behave as a real coverage response, the confidence gradient reversed, and carryover was null (p=0.842). [prior work] attributes this to label or classification error and selection or regression to the mean.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-game shift toward SHOULD-counter play types as evidence of PPP gain
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact with a selection or regression-to-the-mean limitation. The SWITCH subgroup reversed sign across runs, so the pooled advantage did not hold across subgroups.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-scheme re-test of adapters vs wrong-way teams controlling for early-third PPP quintiles
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive with mechanism unclear. Quintile gaps changed sign and the carryover gaps were not clearly positive, so the effect could not be separated from noise or confounding.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Surviving-lift test of a TOV_FORCE channel under opponent re-route, PT-shift and follow-the-ball counters
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as not a hypothesis test with a descriptive verdict. Net lifts were model-implied, not observed; the counter stage was often additive at n<10; sample was 4 games and 8 sides.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project studies of counter or adaptation effects in this data (A1, SHOULD-counter, TOV_FORCE) produced lifts that shrank, reversed, or failed under falsification controls, so raw play-type lift is not sufficient evidence of a counter.
Retrieved records repeatedly flag label or classification error, selection and regression to the mean, and mechanical-floor risk as threats to counter-effect claims in this project's data.
No retrieved record tests the PULL_UP-after-PNR-fail counter claim itself, or defines the unit-level lift threshold of the present question.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP after a PNR fail has a positive lift in the league as a whole.
Whether the 70% and 2pp thresholds are reasonable or correctly calibrated for this comparison.
The unit-level variance of PULL_UP lift, or the power of a test with the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data.
Anything about the 2025-26 playoff data, which is partial before 2026-06-21.
own_inferences: The question is answerable in principle: play-by-play, play-type possession records and matchup data cover the trigger (PNR), the response (PULL_UP) and the outcome (points).

The question as posed is under-specified. 'Unit' (team, team-season, lineup or scheme) and 'PNR fail' (defensive-scheme classification or a play-level outcome) must be fixed before any threshold can be evaluated.

Team-season units give enough possessions for a lift estimate, but per-unit noise may be large enough that 'lift>0 in 70% of units' is driven by sampling noise unless a shrinkage or interval rule is used.

The three artifact-type records suggest the most likely failure mode for this claim is a construction flaw (trigger labelling, selection on early performance, or regression to the mean), not a true null.
uncertainties: [prior work] do not show whether PNR-fail trigger labels exist in the derived play-type records or must be built from the play-by-play.
Retrieval returned no record directly on PULL_UP, PNR fail or the 70%/2pp threshold. Only related A1, SHOULD-counter and TOV_FORCE families came back, and their topics differ.
The 2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13 and the 2025-26 playoffs only from 2026-06-21, so a partial snapshot would change the sample.
Power and effect sizes are not established by any retrieved record.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved evidence did not answer the question, but it changed the design. Because earlier counter-effect claims in this project were recorded as artifact or inconclusive under selection, label-error and regression-to-the-mean checks, the plan adds pre-registered falsification (placebo triggers, pre-trigger lift, carryover and a held-out season) and a shrinkage-based unit rule. Without this evidence the design would have relied on the raw threshold rule alone.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR-fail trigger and PULL_UP labels must be built from play-by-play and checked against the play-type records; mislabelled possessions can create the lift.
Per-unit possession counts for PULL_UP after PNR fail may be too small to estimate lift per unit with a 2pp threshold without pooling or shrinkage.
Selecting trigger possessions by early outcome or by a later result can produce regression-to-the-mean lift, as the retrieved artifact records show.
Shot quality, personnel, score state, clock and opponent defence confound the PULL_UP vs other-action comparison.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record addresses PULL_UP as a counter to PNR fail or the 70%/2pp unit threshold. The cited families study adaptation and counter claims with related designs; their recorded outcomes are artifact, inconclusive, artifact and not a hypothesis test. They are relevant as cautionary precedents about construction and selection flaws, not as answers to this question.

risks.text: Misclassified PNR-fail or PULL_UP possessions could produce spurious lift; retrieved artifact records flag this risk.
Units selected for high or low early lift will regress; selection on the outcome inflates apparent counter effects.
A floor on PPP or shot value from the scoring mechanics can create apparent lift; flagged in the retrieved artifact record.
Unit-level samples may be too small for a per-unit sign test, so the 70% rule may reflect noise.
PNR-fail and PULL_UP possessions may be rare for some teams or seasons, leaving empty or unstable cells.
Shot quality, personnel, score state and opponent scheme differ across PULL_UP and other-action possessions.
Testing several counter candidates or several unit definitions inflates false positives.
If the result depends on one unit definition or one placebo trigger, the claim is not robust.
Defensive schemes and shot selection changed across 2022-23 to 2025-26; pooling may hide season-level reversal.

design.estimand: Within-unit difference in points per possession (PPP) for offensive possessions that use PULL_UP immediately after a PNR fail, minus PPP for matched possessions with the same trigger and another action, averaged over units. The claim is supported only if the 70% and 2pp rules hold on the pre-registered definitions.
design.unit: Offensive team-season (primary); team-season-half and lineup as sensitivity checks. Scheme-level units are excluded from the primary test because they require an inferred-scheme label that the artifact records flag as error-prone.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 (complete from 2026-04-13); playoffs reported separately. Exclude 2025-26 playoffs unless complete (from 2026-06-21). Snapshot date 2026-05-23 for the 2025-26 regular season is partial, so the primary analysis waits for the complete season or uses only games through 2026-04-13 and is labelled as such.
design.power: Not yet established. Before running, simulate per-unit possession counts and the variance of lift; require at least a stated power (e.g., 80%) to detect a 2pp median lift across units. If power is low, report the result as uncertain rather than running the 70% test.
design.controls: Regress PPP on trigger-action indicator with fixed effects for season, team, period, score margin bucket, clock bucket, shot-distance bucket, shooter identity, and opponent defensive matchup minutes. Use pre-trigger PPP as a covariate to address regression to the mean. Trigger labels built from play-by-play, with a random audit of labels against the play-type records.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo trigger: same test with a non-PNR-fail trigger, which should show no lift. (2) Pre-trigger lift: PULL_UP lift before the PNR-fail event should be near zero. (3) Held-out season: estimate on 2022-23 to 2024-25 and test on 2025-26 regular season. (4) Carryover: next-possession PPP should not show the lift if it is a coverage artifact.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary unit definition, one trigger definition and one primary threshold test. Report placebo and sensitivity results as secondary, with Holm correction across the counter candidates tested.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if (a) PULL_UP lift is positive in at least 70% of team-season units, (b) the median unit lift exceeds 2pp with a bootstrap 95% CI above 2pp, (c) the placebo trigger and pre-trigger lift are not significantly different from zero, and (d) the held-out season replicates the sign. Otherwise report artifact if (c) or (d) fails with the lift present, rejected if the lift is near zero and powered, and uncertain if power is inadequate.
design.data_version: Data snapshot as of 2026-05-23. Regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 complete; 2025-26 regular season used only as the held-out season and only from games through 2026-04-13 unless the complete season is available; 2025-26 playoffs excluded (partial before 2026-06-21). Derived play-type records and play-by-play frozen at the analysis date and versioned.
